summary: This is a fragment of a Maven `pom.xml` file that adds the Mockito library to the project. Mockito lets tests create stand-in "mock" objects, such as a fake TemperatureSensor that returns whatever reading the test needs, instead of relying on real hardware.

lines.text: Everything the project needs from outside libraries is listed inside this one element, and Maven downloads each entry for you.
An XML comment marking where the existing JUnit 5 entry sits; the book omits its details here so the new addition stands out.
Opens the description of one single library. Each library needs its own `dependency` block.
The group ID identifies the organization that publishes the library, which keeps two projects with the same name from colliding.
The artifact ID names the specific library within that group; `mockito-core` holds the mocking engine and the `mock()` and `when()` methods.
Pinning an exact version means the build behaves the same today and a year from now, rather than silently picking up changes.
The test scope makes Mockito available when compiling and running tests only, so it is never bundled into the shipped application.
